Baldur's Gate sits along the River Chionthar and grew from Balduran's foundation into a trade city where seagoing ships reach Gray Harbor.
Heroes places patriars in the Upper City, most other people in the Lower City, and refugees and the destitute in the Outer City. Adventures says sturdy walls and gates divide those three districts.
A short way east of Baldur's Gate is the walled district of Little Calimshan, a neighborhood of immigrants from Calimshan.
The Council of Four has three dukes and one grand duke. It enacts laws, directs the Flaming Fist and the navy, and collects taxes. Its authority is not limited to trade law.

Ulder Ravengard is the current grand duke of the Council of Four and remains supreme marshal of the Flaming Fist. He works at both the government duties and the military command. Adventures says he has led the city through recent tribulations, and that his inattention while occupied as grand duke has let the company slide further into oppression and brutality, and into heavy-handed bullying and corruption.
Adventures in Faerûn names the other council members as Duke Dillar Portyr, Duke Brevek Faenor, and Duke Belynne Stelmane.
The Parliament of Peers has fifty politicians, mostly patriars. It meets in the High Hall, recommends policy, and does not enact laws. The council often follows those recommendations.

The Watch is paid by the patriars, based in the Watch Citadel, and keeps the Upper City. At dusk it expels people who lack residence, a designated-guest status, or authorization as a servant. Those who remain carry a Watch token. A resident without a token is also put out.
The Council of Four pays the Flaming Fist to defend the city, patrol its streets, and punish lawbreakers.
The Flaming Fist is headquartered at the Seatower of Balduran, a fortress in Gray Harbor.
The Flaming Fist defers to the Watch for enforcement in the Upper City.
The Flaming Fist is most active in the Lower City.
The Flaming Fist rarely patrols the Outer City, and then in large numbers for a specific goal.
The Flaming Fist staffs Wyrm's Rock to collect taxes and to raise the bridges of Wyrm's Crossing at night.
The Guild is the principal local criminal syndicate in Baldur's Gate. It operates throughout the city and thrives in the Lower City.
Nine-Fingers Keene, a nondescript human, leads the Guild and keeps the organization discreet.
Nine-Fingers directs the Guild toward visitors, nobles, and people who thwart its schemes, and toward a lighter touch on hardworking locals.

Inner gates include Baldur's Gate and the Patriar Gates: Gond Gate, Heap Gate, Manor Gate, and Sea Gate. Outer gates include Basilisk Gate, Black Dragon Gate on the road north toward Waterdeep, Citadel Gate into Citadel Streets, and Cliffgate toward Tumbledown.
Patriars are the elite families of the Upper City. Their manors are opulent town houses. Some secrets are real and some are rumor. A secret of one house is not a fact about every house.
Bane, Bhaal, and Myrkul, the Dead Three, have returned, and their worshipers have resurged in and around Baldur's Gate, hiding in society's shadows and plotting against innocent people.
Adventures says the city's live-and-let-live attitude toward religion allows evil worship, including devil cults, to fester.
The Unrolling Scroll is a temple of Oghma in the Upper City, built around a reflecting pool.
Lady's Hall is the temple of Tymora in the Upper City.

The Water Queen's House is the oldest temple in Baldur's Gate, devoted to Umberlee, and stands at the end of a stone pier in the Lower City docks. It is closed to outsiders. Waveservants at the pier take donations.
Waterdeep and Baldur's Gate are members of the Lords' Alliance, a coalition that keeps trade ties, mutual peace, and common defense while each city keeps its own interests first.
Ulder Ravengard is grand duke and supreme marshal of the Flaming Fist.
The Council of Four directs the Flaming Fist.
The Parliament of Peers advises the council and meets in the High Hall.
The Watch keeps the Upper City, and the Flaming Fist defers to the Watch there.
The Flaming Fist is headquartered at the Seatower of Balduran.
The road from Black Dragon Gate leads north to Waterdeep.
Gray Harbor is Baldur's Gate's port on the Chionthar.
The Guild is Baldur's Gate's principal local criminal organization. Nine-Fingers Keene leads it.
At dusk the Watch clears the Upper City of anyone who is not a resident, a designated guest, or an authorized servant bearing a Watch token. A resident without a token is also removed.
Wyrm's Rock is a Flaming Fist post that collects taxes and raises the bridges of Wyrm's Crossing at night.
The current year is 1501 DR, the Year of the Shining Mythal.

Waterdeep is also called the City of Splendors and is a bustling city.
The Open Lord, Laeral Silverhand, is publicly known. Masked Lords rule beside her anonymously so they cannot be bribed or threatened.
Laeral Silverhand is the current Open Lord of Waterdeep.
Heroes says Waterdeep has a militia and a city guard, and that its most famous defenders are the walking statues and the griffon cavalry. It does not restate the Watch-versus-Guard beat.
Waterdeep's griffon cavalry is made of trained riders and griffon mounts. Each rider wears a ring of feather falling.
Waterdeep's wards are not separated by walls or gates, and crossing between them is easy.
Heroes PDF 98 names Sea Ward, North Ward, Trade Ward, Southern Ward, Dock Ward, the City of the Dead, and the Field Ward outside the normal wards. The wording is include.
Heroes says the Southern Ward is home to many immigrants and the Dock Ward is where many of the poorest live and work.
Heroes of Faerûn spells the same market district Trade Ward.
Heroes forbids a temple or priesthood of Talona in Waterdeep, as with many evil gods. Individuals or families who revere Talona and obey the law are not jailed for that reverence alone.
Heroes says small shrines and temples to strange or newly arrived gods sometimes appear in cosmopolitan cities such as Waterdeep.
Adventurers descend into Undermountain from a well in the Yawning Portal tavern.
Eight enormous walking statues sit dormant among Waterdeep's buildings. The Blackstaff can activate them in dire need.

The Field Ward began as temporary refugee shelters and is now a neighborhood outside the normal city wards. City guards do not patrol it. It has no sanitation or other city services and holds the most desperate citizens.
The City of the Dead is a massive park and open-air mausoleum inside the city, where Waterdeep's dead are entombed.
The wizard holding the office of the Blackstaff is currently Vajra Safahr. Blackstaff Tower is Waterdeep's magical academy.
Undermountain is a twenty-three-floor megadungeon beneath Waterdeep.
Halaster Blackcloak lairs at Undermountain's bottommost level. His motives are described as unknown and perhaps unknowable.
Halaster built Undermountain before Waterdeep was founded and has stocked it with perils.
Other creatures have founded places inside Undermountain, including the city of Skullport.
The Xanathar Guild is a criminal organization operating out of Skullport, and its gang activity spills into Waterdeep.
Skullport is a bustling, crime-ridden subterranean city inside Undermountain, and it is the Xanathar Guild's base.
Laeral Silverhand holds the Open Lordship.
An anonymous Masked Lords council rules beside the Open Lord.
The Yawning Portal well is an entrance to Undermountain.
The Field Ward lies outside routine city-guard patrol.
Vajra Safahr holds the Blackstaff office, which is distinct from the Open Lordship.
